milestone: M12 External Mode Pack Execution Policy

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: External Mode Pack policies can now constrain subtask handoff targets as executable runtime policy rather than prompt-only guidance.
Rust denies disallowed subtask.spawn target modes after permission evaluation but before queueing or child materialization.
Controlled child queues only admit requested child modes that resolve and match the active external mode policy's allowed handoff targets.
ModeResolved persists the bounded handoff allow-list and denial events record only active mode id, requested mode id, reason, and input summary.
Headless callers can rely on replay-safe runtime admission for delegated child work instead of implementing external Mode Pack handoff policy themselves.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances mode_pack_runtime directly, with runtime_permission_enforcement, subtask_orchestration, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development as supporting capabilities.
answers.new_capability: An external Mode Pack mode that can spawn subtasks can declare bounded allowed_handoff_targets, and Rust will admit only those requested child mode ids before queueing.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing can_spawn_subtasks is a broad permission bit. It cannot distinguish which child modes an external orchestrator may hand off to once subtask.spawn is otherwise allowed.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External Mode Packs would be able to request any resolvable child mode allowed by the broad spawn bit, leaving AgentModes-compatible handoff restrictions as unenforced prompt guidance.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M11.1 through M11.3 focused on headless continuation execution and replay. M12.1 changes external Mode Pack execution policy at the subtask admission boundary.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing Mode Pack parser, task.start ModeResolved snapshot, task.run tool-intent evaluation, and subtask queueing path are extended without adding a new RPC.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This stores bounded policy and denial evidence only; it adds no report, digest, history, verdict, readiness wrapper, preview, or summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust rejects a subtask.spawn request when input.mode_id is unknown or absent from the active policy allowed_handoff_targets, and does so before SubtaskOrchestrationQueued or child TaskRecord creation.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless controllers can run external Mode Pack orchestration without reimplementing handoff admission or risking later child materialization from a denied target.
answers.milestone_progress: M12 gains the first concrete external Mode Pack execution-policy enforcement beyond coarse permissions, moving toward safe AgentModes-compatible delegation.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M12.1 changes the deterministic current phase manifest and adds an archived M12.1 manifest. Review must confirm runtime handoff admission behavior, not a wrapper or guard-only phase.

exit_criteria: brownie-modepack accepts allowed_handoff_targets for modes with can_spawn_subtasks=true and rejects missing, duplicate, overlong, or unsupported target ids
ModeResolved persists allowed_handoff_targets and task.run reconstructs them from the ledger policy snapshot
An external mode with allowed_handoff_targets can queue a subtask.spawn request for an admitted child target
An external mode with allowed_handoff_targets denies a resolvable but unlisted subtask.spawn input.mode_id before SubtaskOrchestrationQueued
A denied handoff target cannot later materialize a child TaskRecord on repeated handling or replay
Built-in orchestrator subtask.spawn behavior remains compatible because built-in modes do not declare an allow-list
Denial evidence is bounded and excludes raw prompt, provider response, file content, stdout, stderr, command, environment, path, request body, and secrets
No new RPC, diagnostics wrapper, readiness report, digest, history, preview, or VSIX-owned policy path is added
next_phase_candidate_notes: M12.2 should add a distinct external Mode Pack execution-policy boundary only if it changes runtime behavior, such as controlled child provenance constraints across external pack updates.
next_phase_after_m12_1: M12.2 External Mode Pack Child Provenance Replay Boundary or M12 closeout, depending on remaining milestone gaps
